question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse tool execution mode in agent-core, and must that wait for explicit tool concurrency-safety metadata before early execution is allowed?
rationale: The source-level latency opportunity is real, but the fix changes core runtime scheduling and safety semantics rather than repairing a narrowly broken existing contract.

options.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
options.body: Keep the issue open for an owner design covering scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof.

options.title: Block On Tool Safety Metadata
options.body: Treat this as dependent on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62962 or an equivalent concurrency-safety contract before execution timing changes.

options.title: Defer Runtime Semantics Change
options.body: Keep the current post-stream parallel batching as the only supported behavior if maintainers decide early execution is too risky for now.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open for an owner design covering scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal points to agent-core and provider-stream ownership for the required design decision.
